title: Logical backup success is not persisted into the application catalog or durable manifest
business_impact: The script stores and checks dump bytes, returns an in-memory manifest, prints only status/failure/catalog ID, and exits. The catalog interface has no backup recording operation. A successful job does not create the record read by /system/backups or retain full release/migration/checksum context for discovery and restore. This source gap persists independently of provider runtime availability.
repair_scope: Persist an immutable manifest and application catalog entry with artifact reference/release identity/checksum; define failed-job and catalog-commit reconciliation so artifact-only completion cannot masquerade as a recoverable catalog record.
repair_acceptance: Isolated backup yields one discoverable catalog entry plus durable manifest; process restart preserves it; retrieved bytes match manifest; injected catalog/storage failure does not report complete application backup; explicit isolated restore reproduces DB/files before restore-proven status.

title: Search does not escape the declared LIKE escape character
business_impact: The pattern escapes percent/underscore but not backslash while every ILIKE declares backslash as ESCAPE. Literal searches containing backslash change the next character/wildcard interpretation; e.g. a backslash before percent can restore wildcard behavior within already-authorized rows. This is search correctness, not a demonstrated authorization bypass.
repair_scope: Escape backslash before percent and underscore in a shared literal-LIKE pattern builder; preserve authorization predicates before total/page.
repair_acceptance: PostgreSQL fixture titles containing literal backslash, percent, underscore and combined forms return exact expected authorized rows/counts across cursor pages; foreign-scope controls remain zero.

title: Scheduled backup/drill and worker execution are not wired in the deployment source
business_impact: CalendarBackupScheduler constructs test-environment commands only; monthly drill CLI exits with an isolated-target requirement; render.yaml defines only a web service. The outbox CLI processes one batch and exits. There is no source-wired durable cadence, loop, worker heartbeat or external paging. This does not establish current provider configuration.
repair_scope: After owner approval, wire a durable scheduler/worker execution path with bounded retries, heartbeat, monitored failure and explicit isolated drill target; do not auto-activate billable resources.
repair_acceptance: Restart-safe schedule identity, duplicate tick denial, worker crash/reclaim, backlog drain and heartbeat aging verified; isolated monthly drill and approved failure alert exercised with candidate identity.
